name: slack
description: Slack as a chat provider: the host holds a Socket Mode connection for each connected workspace, and every message the Papercusp app sees (channel posts, mentions, direct messages, the /papercusp command) becomes a chat-message record. A reaction on a message is a `reaction` record of that message, and a message reported through the app's "Report a bug" shortcut (it opens a short form) is a `report` record of it. Workflows can pick channels from the workspace's channel list (chat.channels) and reply in a thread (chat.reply). Made organization-wide, the source also backfills the history of every channel the app is in, and each channel's messages are readable only by that channel's members. With live search switched on, a search reads Slack directly with the searching person's own user token and stores nothing (search.live). Setup is pasted, not OAuth: create the Slack app from the bundled manifest, then paste its app-level token and bot token; each person who searches pastes their own user token.
author: Papercusp

credentials.label: App-level token
credentials.help: Basic Information → App-Level Tokens → Generate Token with the connections:write scope. Papercusp uses it only to open the Socket Mode connection.

credentials.label: Bot token
credentials.help: OAuth & Permissions → Install to Workspace, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token.

credentials.label: Your Slack user token
credentials.help: For live search only, and personal: each person pastes their own. OAuth & Permissions shows the User OAuth Token to whoever installed the app; Slack shows you only what you can already see.
